longForm.heroLead: 12 tubes, stirred at exactly the same speed. Patented, not left to chance. Run 12 reactions on one stirring hotplate and it's easy for stirring speed to drift between positions, some tubes closer to the magnet than others. Carousel 12 Plus doesn't let that happen. Every tube and its stir bar sit equidistant from the hotplate's central magnet, patented specifically to keep stirring identical across all 12 positions, from 100 to 1,400 rpm. Reflux runs through a water-cooled head that removes with the tubes still attached, and the whole system operates under a genuine inert atmosphere: individual gas-tight caps, a radial distribution system, and a two-way stopcock to purge each tube in seconds.

sections.title: Steady-State Design and Circulator Compatibility
body: Holding a temperature steady across hours, not just reaching it once, is what Storm's internal design is actually built around.

The internal fluid path focuses the circulator's thermofluid directly toward the top plate surface, which is what keeps temperature variation minimal across the whole plate rather than concentrated near the inlet. That design pairs with genuinely open circulator compatibility — Huber, Julabo, and Lauda are all named directly, connected via M24 fittings, so you're not locked into one manufacturer's ecosystem to get the full -65°C to +200°C range.

longForm.heroLead: A small internal volume means a fast response. Built to follow a changing temperature, not just hold one. Some reactions need a temperature held steady for hours. Others need it to actually move, precisely, on demand. Breeze is built for the second kind. Its small internal volume is the whole design decision: less thermal mass to shift means faster response when the temperature setpoint changes, which is exactly what crystallisation studies need. Combine it with a circulator and you get a solution temperature of -30°C to +165°C, from a thermofluid range that runs much wider, -85°C to +235°C. The 135 mm top plate fits the Carousel 6 Plus, Tornado, Heat-On, and other reaction blocks, heating or cooling multiple flasks up to 5 litres at once. sections.title: Thermofluid Range, Solution Temperature and Response Time
body: The thermofluid running through Breeze and the temperature your solution actually experiences are two different numbers, and the gap between them is real, not a rounding artifact.

Thermofluid reaches -85°C to +235°C, but by the time that heat or cold transfers through the plate to the solution, the achievable range narrows to -30°C to +165°C. What makes Breeze useful despite that narrower range is speed: its small internal volume means there's less thermal mass to bring along for the ride, so it catches up to a new setpoint faster than a larger, insulated system would.
